context: Reproduce in a fresh pool worktree. Decide whether the skill-sync step should fetch the pinned SHA before checkout, skip with a notice when the tree is unreadable (the target already has a no-op-with-notice path for a missing skill-sync CLI, so the idiom exists), or fail loudly but only after reporting which artifacts were regenerated.
description: Observed 2026-07-30 in a fresh pool worktree: 'make guards-fix' regenerates the earlier artifacts fine (audit-raw, oracle-coverage-map, parity-fixtures, compat-docs, UAT LOC table) and then dies at its skill-sync step with 'Command failed: git checkout a48d0c02884f032b075f5968ab23e1261cf23dbc / fatal: unable to read tree' and exit 2. Because skill-sync is the LAST step (Makefile:810+) the earlier regens do survive, so the failure is recoverable - but the target exits non-zero, which means anyone using it to clear a drift guard sees a failure and cannot tell whether their artifact was regenerated. The referenced SHA is not readable in the worktree, suggesting a skill-sync mirror lock pointing at a commit that was never fetched (or was pruned) there.

preserves.behavior: A genuine skill-sync drift is still surfaced, not silently swallowed
guards-fix still regenerates every other drift-guard artifact

verifications.description: guards-fix completes in a fresh pool worktree
verifications.expected: exit 0, or a clear skip notice naming the unreadable SHA

work_units.summary: Diagnose why the pinned skill-sync tree SHA is unreadable in a fresh worktree
Make the step fetch, skip-with-notice, or fail after reporting regenerated artifacts
